items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: This time, it was with a young French pianist named Claude Bolling... Claude was going to work in the club St. Germain des Prés... he made me two propositions... being a regular member of the band. The last one was moreinteresting for me... and that's the one I went for.

ctx.x: Home was wherever I hung my hat, and I travelled with all my earthly belongings. When Lily and I got together, she had quite a few things also. We had left a few bags in Switzerland and when the gig in Blankenberge fell through, we decided that Lily should do to Switzerland to get the suit-cases we had left there and I would go to Paris with the things we had with us. I left with 11 pieces of luggage, and when I had to change trains in Brussels for one that would bring me to France, the train was so crowded that…

I had always lived in the Pigalle section of Paris and as I had given Lily the address of a hotel on a rue Blanche where we had stayed before, that's where I went to await her arrival. Five days after I arrived, I received an offer through the help of Charles Delaunay, to work at the Club Vieux Colombier, a club I had worked for a while with the Edouard's band and Don Byas. This time, it was with a young French pianist named Claude Bolling. I started the 14th of July which is a National holiday in France, and as…

The corners of Boulevard St. Germain des Prés and rue de Rennes, St. Benoit and St. Germain were the most popular corners of the district, and had very large cafés, where the students,artists and friends met.
